subject: Materials Science
title: Epoxy Matrix: The Standard Binder
description: A micro-lesson that makes Epoxy Matrix: The Standard Binder usable.

hook.text: Carbon fiber is useless yarn without a matrix. Epoxy turns it into an engineering miracle.

buildup.text: Epoxy resin cross-links when mixed with hardener, forming a rigid thermoset around the fibers.

discovery.text: It bonds strongly to fibers, resists chemicals, and shrinks very little during cure.

twist.text: Epoxy is brittle on its own — without fibers it cracks easily under impact.

climax.text: Over 70% of aerospace composites use epoxy matrices — the industry gold standard.

punchline.text: Epoxy holds fibers together and lets them do the heavy lifting.

quiz.question: Why is epoxy the most common composite matrix in aerospace?
options: It is the cheapest polymer available
It bonds well to fibers, resists chemicals, and shrinks little
It is naturally flexible and impact-resistant
